title: Weight residency controller and async load playbook
content:
Purpose
This is a pragmatic, operational playbook and spec for a Weight Residency Controller (WRC) and accompanying async load strategies. Goal: make model weights available to the serving runtime with predictable latency and bounded memory while enabling safe hot-swap and tight integration with KV cache and kernel selection. This doc focuses on behavior (states, transitions), scheduling interactions, and operational knobs rather than micro-optimizations already tracked in other PRs.

Problem statement and context
- We want fast cold-starts for large models without OOMs or long synchronous stalls.
- Workloads vary (many short requests vs few long ones); residency strategy must adapt.
- We maintain multiple binary formats (safetensors, raw flatbuffers, quantized blobs) and multiple memory mappings (mmap for read-only host-residency, pinned GPU allocations for inference).
- Hot-swap (swap model weights or variants at runtime) must preserve correctness (kernel compatibility + KV cache semantics) and degrade gracefully on failure.

Key concepts / vocabulary
- Residency state: UNLOADED, MMAPED_HOST, PARTIAL_GPU_RESIDENT, FULL_GPU_RESIDENT, STREAMING_LOAD_IN_PROGRESS, LOCKED (during hot-swap).
- Loader: component performing I/O + deserialization + device staging. Supports sync and async paths.
- Residency Controller (WRC): orchestrates which tensors should be resident and where. Implements eviction, prefetch, and hot-swap coordination.
- Mapper: maps safetensors/file offsets to page segments and associated tensor identities.
- Eviction Manager: evicts tensors with policy and notifies KV cache where necessary.

High-level strategy
1) Default lazy load: model graph can be instantiated with all tensors UNLOADED. The first request that needs a tensor triggers the WRC decision path: if small/single-shot request, stream missing tensors on-demand; if throughput-critical, prefetch model-critical params (attention, embedding tables) into PARTIAL_GPU_RESIDENT.
2) mmap-first: prefer mmap host-residency for large weight files. If platform supports O_DIRECT + madvise, use those to minimize page faults. mmap acts as a fallback fast-path that avoids upfront allocation.
3) Async background prefetch: WRC runs a predictive prefetcher based on recent token distributions, routes, and KV cache hit-rate heuristics. Prefetch can escalate to full device staging when expected token volume crosses thresholds.
4) Hot-swap path: prepare replacement weights via WRC in MMAPED_HOST state, validate kernel/quantization compat, atomically flip model pointer table, evict old tensors after safe quiesce.

Residency controller behavior (detailed)
- Inputs: model metadata (tensor list, sizes, format, kernel hints), historical request profile, configured memory budget, KV cache metrics.
- Outputs: assignment (for each tensor) -> {target_state, confidence, version_tag, eviction_policy}
- Decision algorithm (simplified):
  * Score each tensor by (access_freq * tensor_importance_factor / size) + kv_cache_correlation_score.
  * Sort and greedily fill GPU budget for PARTIAL_GPU_RESIDENT until marginal score drops below background_load_threshold.
  * Remaining high-scoring tensors get MMAPED_HOST and flagged for async prefetch.

Loading paths and APIs
- sync_load(tensor_id): blocking path used primarily during model init or admin-driven full-load. Returns success or deterministic error.
- async_load(tensor_id, priority, callback_id): enqueue load. Priority levels: realtime, user-foreground, background. Callbacks post completion with residency token.
- stream_load_segment(tensor_id, byte_range, priority): streaming path for giant tensors (e.g., 60B embedding matrices). Supports progressive decoding.

File format handling (safetensors + companions)
- Mapper will build a per-file index: tensor_name -> file_offset, length, dtype, shape, quant_meta (if present).
- For safetensors we rely on file-offset stable mapping: mmap + pointer arithmetic -> avoid extra copy for host-residency. If quantized blobs are present inside safetensors, annotate with 'needs-dequant' so loader schedules GPU dequant path.
- Fallback flow: if safetensors header invalid or missing, attempt raw flat binary; if both fail, mark model as LOAD_FAILED.

mmap policies and heuristics
- Use MADV_SEQUENTIAL for known-onepass loads (e.g., weight streaming at startup). Use MADV_RANDOM for mixed-access workloads.
- On Linux, prefer MAP_POPULATE for immediate page fault reduction when confidence high and budget allows.
- Limit total mmapped bytes per host to avoid swapping pressure; expose softlimit via WRC config. If mmapped bytes exceed limit, prefer streaming smaller segments on-demand.

GPU staging and chunking
- Chunking: break tensors > chunk_threshold into M-sized chunks (configurable, default 32MB) to allow interleaving load+inference.
- Partial GPU residency: keep high-use chunks resident, evict tail chunks first. Maintain a per-tensor LRU on chunk-level.
- Transfers: overlap memcpy + kernel queue submission; use a small window semaphore between loader and inference executor to bound concurrency.

KV cache interactions
- KV cache references weight residency indirectly: for generation-heavy workloads, KV cache hits predict continued use of certain attention layers -> increase their residency confidence.
- When evicting weights, avoid invalidating KV cache unless weight format/version changes. If hot-swap changes kernel semantics, KV cache must be invalidated or remapped. Policy default: if version_tag changes major bit, flush KV cache for that model instance.
- Expose an advisory API: WRC.advisory_on_eviction(tensor, reason) -> KV cache can respond by marking affected prefixes as cold.

Eviction policies and safety
- Tiered eviction: CHUNK_LRU -> TENSOR_LEAST_IMPORTANT -> MMAP_RELEASE.
- Eviction must respect LOCKED state (hot-swap in progress). Eviction requests for LOCKED tensors are queued and retried after quiesce.
- Eviction callback must provide window for active requests: 30s soft-grace by default, configurable per-model. If requests persist beyond grace, force-evict only if memory pressure critical.

Hot-swap protocol (safe replacement)
1) Admin triggers swap with new model bundle (or variant) and target version_tag.
2) WRC preloads new bundle into MMAPED_HOST and performs compatibility checks: shape mismatches, required fused kernels availability, quantization bitwidth.
3) If compatibility checks pass, prepare delta plan: tensors to stage into GPU, tensors to reuse, and tensors to retire.
4) Acquire per-model swap LOCK (prevents further cross-model route migrations). Wait for in-flight requests to hit quiesce point (max wait config). Optionally serve from fallback smaller model or previous variant during quiesce.
5) Atomically update pointer table used by executor (single memory barrier + version bump). Release LOCK.
6) Background eviction of retired tensors. Report metrics and rollout status.

Kernel and compilation checks
- Each model variant lists required kernel features (e.g., fused_attention_v2, qint8_kernels). At preload time, verify runtime kernel registry can satisfy requirements; else mark as "requires-fallback" and optionally enable slower kernels.
- For quantized tensors, ensure kernel supports the specific scale/zero-point layout; otherwise convert during preload (adds CPU->GPU work).

Scheduling and runtime integration
- The WRC exposes priorities; Request scheduler tags requests with urgency. WRC uses urgency to bump tensor priority for immediate load.
- Backpressure: if many high-priority loads are queued, scheduler will temporarily reject low-priority background prefetch tasks.
- Admission control: refuse to accept new large model startups if memory headroom insufficient; return a 503 with a structured reason that can be surfaced to customers.

Metrics and telemetry (required)
- Per-model: resident_bytes_host, resident_bytes_gpu, avg_load_latency_ms (sync and async), stream_throughput_bytes_s, evictions_count, hot_swap_success_rate.
- Per-tensor: last_access_ts, access_rate_per_min, chunk_residency_fraction.
- Traces: attach loader spans to request traces (so load-induced tail latency links to request).

Operational runbook (quick steps)
- OOM during load: kill in-progress background loads, reduce per-model GPU budget, roll back recent hot-swap, mark model unhealthy and redirect traffic.
- Hot-swap failure at pointer flip: auto-roll back to previous pointer table and surface error with diagnostic bundle (mmap files, kernel registry snapshot).
- Slow initial inference after deploy: investigate mmap faults (high major fault rate), enable MAP_POPULATE on suspect files, or increase async prefetch aggressiveness.

Bench experiments to run
- Compare mmap vs streaming for embedding-heavy models (64B tokens) with various page sizes and chunk sizes.
- Latency tail when hot-swap with prewarm vs without prewarm across p99.9.
- Impact of chunk size on throughput for 4xA100 vs 8xA100 setups.

Open questions / TODOs
- How to safely migrate on-the-fly between quantization schemes without full KV cache invalidation? Research: per-token re-embedding patching?
- Should we persist a lightweight residency manifest in S3 for faster control-plane rehydration? (pros: faster restart; cons: staleness risk).
- Implement a simulated load generator to validate prefetch heuristics under mixed workloads (short chat queries + long completions).

References and links
- RFC: incremental-weight-streaming (internal) RED-2901 (see linked artifacts)
- PR: safetensors-adapter with file-indexing (github PR in linked_artifacts)

Notes to reviewers
- This doc intentionally focuses on the orchestration layer and operational playbook. Low-level kernel optimizations (attn kernels, fused dequant) are tracked separately; ensure compatibility checks cover those PRs.
- If we accept the proposed prioritization logic, implementing a lightweight simulator first will reduce surprises in production.

Last updated notes
- 2025-12-02: Updated hot-swap protocol to include explicit pointer table swap and added eviction grace semantics.

Action items
- [ ] Add simulation harness ticket (RED-3418)
- [ ] Wire WRC metrics to ModelConsole per-model page (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Prototype chunked streaming for one mid-size model and capture p95/p99 before wider rollout (owner: Liam)
